title: Rate Administration Rule — Assigning and Changing the Schedule of an Electric Service by Rate Schedule Account
content:
## Assignment

Each Electric Service by Rate Schedule account is assigned the one rate schedule whose entry limits the location satisfies:

- the service phase must match the phase the schedule accepts ("either" accepts both);
- the installed transformer capacity may not exceed the schedule's largest transformer;
- the expected maximum demand from the application must lie from the schedule's lowest through its highest expected demand, both inclusive;
- a schedule that requires a permanent residence serves only the member's year-round primary residence;
- a schedule that requires agricultural use serves only agricultural production load.

Where two schedules both fit — for example, a farm residence that also meets Schedule R — the member chooses, and the choice stands until a rate change.

## Changing schedules

**Waiting period.** A rate schedule change may take effect only after the schedule's rate change waiting period, in full calendar months, has passed since the current rate schedule took effect. The record that starts the clock is the account's rate effective date. Calendar months are counted from the rate effective date to the same day number of the later month, falling back to the last day of that month when the day number does not exist. The day on which the last full month completes satisfies the waiting period; any earlier day does not.

**Effective date of a change.** A change takes effect on the first day of the next billing period, and the new rate effective date is that day.

**Forced change.** A change forced by the location no longer meeting the current schedule's entry limits — demand grown past the schedule's highest expected demand, a three-phase upgrade — is made at the next billing period regardless of the waiting period.

**Consequences of the schedule.** The schedule assigned decides whether the account may join Budget Billing or PrePay Power, which security deposit tier is assessed, and the capital credit patron class into which its patronage is allocated.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates, 12-month waiting period)

| Rate effective date | Waiting period complete on | Change effective that day | Change effective the day before |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-04-15 | 2026-04-15 | Permitted | Not permitted |
| 2024-02-29 | 2025-02-28 (no 29th; last day of February) | Permitted | Not permitted |
| 2025-08-31 | 2026-08-31 | Permitted | Not permitted |

A member-requested change cannot take effect on a day before the date in the second column; a forced change for an account whose demand has outgrown its schedule is not held to that date.
